editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 11 October
editions.lede: Four Iranian delegations came to Kabul this week. None of them came to discuss the 492,000 Afghans Iran has deported this year.

items.headline: Tehran sent four delegations to Kabul in five days
items.gist: 5-9 Oct: Iranian parliamentary delegation, 180 traders under the Joint Chamber, energy minister Aliabadi on ~2,000MW, and Zanganeh with the Herat/Farah/Nimroz governors. Iran set aside ~110 hectares at Chabahar (10 in port, 100 in the free zone); talk of $10bn trade; Kabul promised 24-hour opening at Islam Qala, Abu Nasr Farahi and Nimroz. Nothing signed. Iran is 32.9% of imports and 31.1% of exports in FY2026 to date (World Bank, Aug).

items.headline: Iran has deported 492,300 Afghans so far this year
items.gist: UNHCR, 8 Oct: 581,600 returns from Iran 1 Jan-3 Oct, of which 492,300 forced (85%); 475,400 arrived after 28 Feb. 2025 comparison: 1.9m returns, ~1.26m forced. Remittances fell from 17.8% to 15.7% of GDP, the World Bank attributing most of the drop to the returns.

items.headline: Kabul now buys by the barrel what it used to pull from the ground
items.gist: CNN, 6 Oct: one household pays 150 AFN ($2.35) a day for seven people. Water table down ~100 feet in a decade; about half the city's boreholes dry; one well past 700 feet; extraction exceeds recharge by 44m cubic metres a year; one in five has piped water; poorer households spend up to 30% of income against a UN benchmark of 3%. Shahtoot dam never broke ground; the 124-mile Panjshir pipeline is still at survey. Prosper Global puts day zero as early as 2030.

items.headline: Trade with Russia is up by half again, and barely any of it comes back the other way
items.gist: Figures released 7 Oct: Afghan-Russian trade +150% in the first seven months of 2026. Russian customs put 2025 at ~$326m, Afghan figures at ~$590m; on the Russian numbers 2026 lands near $815m. Afghan exports to Russia about $4m. Russia supplied 4.7% of Afghan imports in FY2026 to August.

editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 18 October
editions.lede: Afghan farmers have just had a good year. Nineteen million Afghans will still go short this winter.

items.headline: The harvest came in strong. The hunger forecast got worse.
items.gist: IPC analysis published 13 Oct: 15.9m (32%) in Phase 3+ now, of which 3.4m Phase 4; Nov 2026-Apr 2027 projection 19.2m (38%) including 5m Phase 4, nearly double the Apr-Sep projection and ~0.5m above last winter; May-Sep 2027 falls back to 15.3m (30%). Seven provinces projected into Phase 4: Daykundi, rural Ghazni, Badakhshan, Samangan, Sar-e-Pul, Badghis, Ghor. Malnutrition caseload 4.04m children in 2027 (+9%), SAM 1.095m (up from 942,000), 1.27m pregnant and breastfeeding women, 3.9m stunted. A third of nutrition sites closed or suspended; food aid expected to reach ~1% of the population in the lean season. Strong 2026 cereal harvest; the binding constraint is wages, not supply. WFP market report for the first week of October: work found 2 days/week (-14% y/y), day wage 295 AFN (-5%), buying power -25% y/y and -30% v three-year average; rice +31%, oil +12%, flour +10%; diesel 80.9 AFN/l; urea +24%; AFN 64.9/USD. FEWS NET's new outlook is less alarming: Phase 3 in six provinces plus urban centres, above-average winter precipitation and above-average winter wheat area.

items.headline: A year with the border shut, and the stand-in only works one way
items.gist: Mujahid claimed on 14 Oct that Central Asian trade has offset the closed Pakistani crossings. Kazakh figures show substitution on the import side only: Jan-Jul 2026 bilateral trade $581.1m, of which $572.9m Kazakh exports and $8.2m Afghan exports (70:1); flour $215.6m, wheat $122m, vegetable oil $51.1m; grain and flour volumes up ~54-58% to about 2m tonnes. On 13 Oct ten Afghan companies signed five contracts in Kazakhstan worth $55m ($40m wheat and farm goods, $15m flour) - all purchases. Export side unreplaced: Afghan transit through Pakistan $6.7bn in 2023 v $367m this fiscal year; containers 42,959 in FY24-25 v 11,592. Fruit to India now $0.70-0.80 per unit and two months via Iran, against $0.25 and 10-15 days via Pakistan; one Kabul trader $350,000 down on apples and grapes. Customs duties fell 24.7% y/y in the fiscal year to June. Crossings closed 12 Oct 2025; Torkham, Chaman, Ghulam Khan, Kharlachi and Angoor Adda still shut to goods.

items.headline: The transit line is nearly built. The buyer at the far end is Pakistan.
items.gist: DABS said this week the Afghan section of CASA-1000 is 70% complete, finishing end of 1406 (March 2028). Project: ~$1.2bn, 1,300 MW from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan via Kabul to Nowshera, split 1,000 MW Pakistan / up to 300 MW Afghanistan; Kabul expects $60-65m a year in wheeling fees. Joint working group met in Bishkek 7-9 Oct; Kyrgyz section finished Nov 2024 (456 km, 1,243 towers); World Bank's January update expected whole-project completion by end-2027. Discrepancy unexplained: the Afghan section was put at ~75% complete in Oct 2025 and is now 70%. No payment mechanism published for a wheeling fee from Pakistan, whose crossings are shut and whose air force struck Kunar and Helmand on 1 Oct. On 3 Oct Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and the UAE signed an MoU to study a ~900 km railway to Pakistani ports through Afghanistan; Afghanistan was not a signatory.

items.headline: The money for weather stations sits behind a recognition problem
items.gist: Baradar, deputy PM for economic affairs, spoke in Kabul on 13 Oct for the International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction, asking for meteorological equipment, early-warning systems and rescue gear and calling Afghanistan's exclusion 'completely inconsistent with the principles of international climate justice'. Mechanism: the big funds accredit national entities, and accreditation runs through a recognised government. Afghanistan's whole Green Climate Fund book is $17.2m across one project (FP129, approved Aug 2020, UNDP) plus $1.6m readiness; no new multilateral climate approval since 2021. Workaround routes around the state: FAO ($10m) and UNDP ($8.9m) proposals to the GEF, still awaiting its council at the last public account. Donor reluctance ties back to restrictions on women working, which the IPC lists as a hunger driver.

editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 25 October
editions.lede: Afghanistan's finance ministry began designing a stock market this week. The money that actually holds the country up arrives by hand, from men who are being deported.

items.headline: Kabul starts drawing up a stock market
items.gist: 22 Oct: finance ministry's first meeting on establishing a capital market, ordered by the Taliban leader. Chaired by Finance Minister Mullah Mohammad Nasir Akhund, with Commerce Minister Nooruddin Azizi and DAB governor Haji Noor Ahmad Agha; treasury DG Nasratullah Mahmood presented. Stated aim: turn 'idle capital' into investment in industry and infrastructure. No law, regulator or timetable announced. Context: World Bank Enterprise Survey 2025 found banks financed 0.28% of Afghan firms' investment (MENA 9.8%; Afghanistan 1.5% in 2014), under 1% of working capital; access to finance the top constraint; 32% of women-led firms fully credit-constrained v 16% of male-led.

items.headline: Two trains, and a headline that needs correcting
items.gist: 21 Oct: freight train left Linyi, Shandong, for Hairatan with 8m yuan (~$1.1m) of textiles, chemical feedstock, tools and construction machinery; route Khorgos–Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan–Termez, 20 days, due ~10 Nov. Widely reported as the first direct China–Afghanistan freight train; in fact a Chongqing–Hairatan direct service ran its first train 10 Feb 2025 (55 FEU, 12–15 days, ZTE equipment), so this is the first from Shandong. Westbound: 22 Oct the public works ministry said 600 tonnes of cotton left for Türkiye via the Khaf–Herat railway through Iran (no value, no exporter named). Herat chamber of commerce: exports through Islam Qala ~$124m in H1 2026, +72% y/y, ~1,000 lorries a day, ~6,000 staff; prior-year figure in the same statement does not reconcile (flagged by Pajhwok).

items.headline: Pakistan arrested 86,644 Afghans this year, then sent most of them home
items.gist: UNHCR–IOM joint flash update 115, published 24 Oct, covering 1 Jan–17 Oct 2026: 86,644 Afghans arrested or detained in Pakistan, of whom 82,526 ACC-holders or undocumented and 4,118 PoR-holders or asylum seekers. Balochistan 55% of cases; Chaghi district alone 35,740. Returns from Pakistan 812,131 in 2026, including 85,821 deportees — about one in ten. Week to 17 Oct: 517 arrests (-47%), 3,883 returns via Torkham, Chaman and Bahramcha including 499 deportees (-48%). Since 1 Apr 2025 nearly 1.9m returns incl 237,387 deportations; since Sep 2023 2.74m incl 278,758. IOM July survey: 96% of returnees from Pakistan cited fear of arrest. Agencies say arrest counts are likely undercounts.

items.headline: Donors met in Doha to discuss life after aid
items.gist: Afghanistan Coordination Group met in Doha 20–21 Oct. Qatar's minister of state for international cooperation, Maryam bint Ali bin Nasser Al Misnad, pressed for a shift from emergency relief to economic recovery and private-sector development, and better donor coordination; OIC delegation set out girls' education, food security and counterterrorism. Qatar has given or pledged ~$150m over a decade. Nothing decided, nothing newly pledged. Three days later the Shelter and Non-Food Items Cluster asked for $12.8m for 102 priority districts Oct 2026–Mar 2027, including cash for 198,832 people; the 2026 appeal stands at 31.38% of $1.71bn.

explainer.topic: Wages earned somewhere else: remittances as the country's largest dependable foreign-currency inflow (15.7% of GDP in FY2025, down from 17.8%, roughly $3bn on a $20.3bn economy, about six times what the 2026 appeal has raised), how they travel outside the banking system through a hawala dealer and a code for a 1–3% fee, who receives them (15% of rural households, about a fifth of their spending; the main income for 5% of the population), and why deporting a worker ends the income rather than relocating it — the wage stops, a consumer arrives, and he enters a market paying 300 afs for 2.0 days' work a week, about $37 a month against a 1,700 afs sack of flour

editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 1 November
editions.lede: Poppy pays in cash, at the farm gate, on the day. Very little else in Afghanistan settles that easily.
sections: How It Works — The Missing Correspondent

items.headline: Four years after the ban, the poppy is back
items.gist: UNODC survey published Thu 29 Oct: poppy area 43,300 ha in 2026, up from about 10,200 in 2025 (+325-330%); production about 1,466 t from 296 t (+~400%); yield 33.8 kg/ha from 29. Poppy in 16 of 34 provinces, five more than 2025. North-east 76% of area (~33,000 ha, ~1,090 t): Badakhshan 6,600 to ~29,500 ha, Takhar 274 to ~3,400; Helmand 681 to ~3,500, Kandahar ~1,560 (from ~500). Dried opium $500/kg, down from $570, against under $100 pre-ban; more than 200,000 ha before the ban. UNODC estimate of income inside Afghanistan about $525m, 2.7% of GDP and 8.5% of agriculture (reported by Amu TV). Per-hectare gross about $16,900 for poppy against roughly $1,000 for wheat at 28 AFN/kg. Interior ministry rejected it: spokesman Mufti Abdul Mateen Qani said cultivation near zero and more than 26,000 ha cleared and asked UNODC for satellite dates, coordinates and error margins; other accounts of the ministry's position give ~24,000 ha cultivated and 22,000-23,000 ha eradicated. UNODC says it cannot verify the eradication claim.

items.headline: The state counted its exports, and a sixth were missing
items.gist: NSIA figures announced Tue 27 Oct for the first six months of 1405 (late March to late September 2026): exports $598.5m, down $125.7m (17.4%) from $724.2m; imports $6,656.6m, up $116.3m from $6,540.3m; gap about $6.06bn, roughly 11:1. Exports: fresh and dried fruit $223.5m (37.3%), medicinal plants $136.9m (22.9%), minerals $32.1m, seeds $12.5m. Imports: petroleum and oils $1,399m (21%), machinery and vehicles $765m (11.5%), metals $691.3m, wheat and flour $554m, vegetable oil $240.8m. Pakistan's TDAP data via Dawn (reported 19 Oct): bilateral trade down 74% to $358m from $1.3bn; Afghan transit 11,592 containers worth $367m against about 89,000 worth ~$5bn pre-2021. Import substitution: Baradar opened phase one of the Shorandam cement plant, Kandahar, Thu 29 Oct, 1,500 t/day heading for 5,000, investment put at $113m by the mines ministry in September, three phases, about 500 on site.

items.headline: A hundred thousand visitors, and 184 million afghanis
items.gist: Afghanistan's first mining exhibition, Kabul International Exhibition Centre, 28-31 Oct: 150 stands, companies from China, India and Iran, more than 100,000 visitors per ministry spokesman Humayun Afghan. Mines minister Hedayatullah Badri, 28 Oct: about 350 active mining contracts, 44 large-scale; about 180,000 people employed in mining; 1,510 precious-stone licences, 1,287 of them in Kunduz, Takhar and Badakhshan. Sideline auction of Panjshir emeralds, Kabul rubies, Kunar tourmaline and Nuristan kunzite raised 184m AFN (about $2.8m). Four MoUs signed, all domestic companies, none named, no values. Iran's acting charge d'affaires Ali Reza Bikdeli attended. Pipeline context: $200m 25-year contract with Delta International Energy (Saudi) signed 7 Sep for seven blocks of the 22,000 sq km Kushk-Tirpul basin in Herat and Badghis, 8-year exploration period; $38.74m 15-year talc contract signed 24 Oct for 3.93 sq km at Woch Bandar, Achin district, Nangarhar, about 400 jobs. Minerals earned only $32.1m of exports in six months. Afghan Witness counted at least 205 contracts to 150+ companies Aug 2021-Feb 2024, ministry a shareholder in at least nine; ACLED at least eight armed clashes over Badakhshan gold mines since 2021.

items.headline: Karachi begins selling the cargo it would not let through
items.gist: Pajhwok reported Sun 25 Oct that Pakistani customs had begun auctioning Afghan traders' containers at Karachi port; traders confirmed it to the agency. Reports say hundreds of containers; no official statement, no count, no value, no legal basis published. Afghanistan-Pakistan Joint Chamber says more than 60% of stranded goods have been returned to origin or rerouted to Chabahar and Bandar Abbas, the rest tangled in fee and paperwork disputes. Earlier chamber claims of up to 15,000 Afghan containers at Pakistani ports remain unconfirmed. Afghan chamber officials called the auctions contrary to regional and international trade law. Mechanism noted: demurrage and storage charges accrue daily, and once they plus unpaid duties exceed cargo value customs may sell to recover the debt. Sourcing is secondhand and agency-fed.

explainer.topic: The missing correspondent: why a cross-border payment is two bookkeeping entries guaranteed by a third bank, what a correspondent and a nostro account are, why large banks de-risked out of Afghanistan rather than being forbidden to act (a European bank needing 40-50 staff for one transaction; an Afghan bank smuggling cash after failing for years to pay a US supplier $3m), why Da Afghanistan Bank cannot vouch for its banks (governor on a UN list, about $7bn frozen in 2021 with half in a Swiss trust now around $4.2bn and never disbursed, APG membership inactive since 2022), what a $3.5bn banking system with private credit at 2.5% of GDP and 0.28% of firm investment bank-financed can actually do, and the three routes that remain - physical cash including the UN's $2.9bn-plus of flown-in banknotes, hawala netting at 1-3%, and third-country trading intermediaries - all of which suit small, physical, repeated transactions and none of which finances an eight-year drilling programme

editions.title: Kabul Ledger — 8 November
editions.lede: A Dubai property developer now holds thirty years of Afghan gas.

items.headline: A property developer takes thirty years of Afghan gas
items.gist: Wed 4 Nov: Ministry of Mines and Petroleum signed two 30-year contracts with the Azizi Group, a Dubai conglomerate (Azizi Energy is a wholly owned Dubai subsidiary; chairman Mirwais Azizi, CEO Jawed Ludin). Gas: Jangal-e-Kalan field, Jawzjan, >3,000 sq km of the Amu Darya basin. Coal: 111 sq km around Pul-e-Khumri, Baghlan. Mines minister Hedayatullah Badri put investment at $275m, the state share at 75% of gas extracted plus a 15% royalty, 1,000MW of generation and about 2,000 jobs — all of that from The Kabul Tribune alone. Khaama reported the same ceremony saying the value was NOT disclosed and putting jobs near 5,000 across both projects; Amu carried $275m but no revenue share. Bakhtar, 7 Nov, described the Baghlan side separately via the deputy PM's office: five coal mines, 69.4m tonnes, annual revenues estimated ~$60m, no mention of Azizi or a signing. Azizi's wider Afghan book: Feb 2026 five DABS generation contracts, 845MW, ~$463m (330MW solar in Kabul/Parwan/Ghazni, 165MW coal Takhar, 350MW coal Baghlan); Aug 2026 Shanghai Electric agreement for 3,000MW over four years; stated target 10,000MW. Nothing commissioned; solar reported under construction at Ghazni, Naghlu, Barikab. Afghanistan imports close to 80% of its power. Baradar met Mirwais Azizi on 4 Nov.

items.headline: Bank Alfalah sells up and goes home
items.gist: Reported 7 Nov (Dawn, Ariana, Khaama; Pajhwok 8 Nov): Pakistan's Bank Alfalah told shareholders on Friday it had fully exited Afghanistan after 20 years, selling its local banking business to Ghazanfar Bank. Transaction completed 5 Nov after definitive documents and approval from the State Bank of Pakistan and Da Afghanistan Bank; disclosed via a PSX notice. Alfalah opened in Kabul in 2005, conventional and Islamic banking; Khaama says Kabul and Herat branches, a non-binding offer in Dec 2025, preliminary regulatory approval in Jan 2026, customers told to move balances or withdraw by 2 Nov. No sale price, no stated reason, no mention of sanctions or de-risking in any coverage. Unknown and worth establishing: whether any foreign-parented bank still operates in Afghanistan.

items.headline: Pine nuts are selling. Almost nothing else is.
items.gist: ACCI via Ariana, 2 Nov: pine nut exports up 69% in the first seven months of solar year 1405, to $72m from $42m; mostly China, some Europe and India. Set against NSIA's six-month figures (27 Oct): total exports $598.5m, down 17.4% or $126m, with fruit and medicinal plants about two thirds of the remainder — periods differ, so the two do not net cleanly. Second trade number: the UK Department for Business and Trade factsheet released 6 Nov (via Ariana, 7 Nov) shows UK-Afghanistan trade in goods and services down 16.7% to £70m in the 12 months to end-June 2026, a £14m fall. UK exports to Afghanistan £57m (-18.6%); imports £13m (-7.1%); goods £32m (45.7%), services £38m (54.3%); leading Afghan goods export to the UK vegetables and fruit at £1.7m. Afghanistan is the UK's 166th-largest trading partner, under 0.1% of UK trade.

items.headline: In Ghazni, the salt plant runs three days in ten
items.gist: Amu TV, 3 Nov, interviewing plant managers in Ghazni. A salt factory's output fell from 200-300 sacks a day to 20-30; manager Bashir Ahmad says workers are called in once every three or four days. A mineral water plant cut staff from 20-25 to six to eight (manager Siyar Ahmad). Paint factory manager Hamidullah Munib wants higher tariffs on imported paint; carpet manager Hussaindad Rezaei says weavers cannot sell handmade wool. The group's asks were electricity, industrial parks and market access, not aid. Context: NSIA half-year imports $6,656.6m against exports $598.5m.

explainer.topic: What a thirty-year resource contract pays this year: why a contract announcement is a spending promise and not a payment ($275m over 30 years is about $9m a year, roughly twenty cents per Afghan); what a royalty is (a slice of output, not of profit, so the state is paid whether or not the company prospers) and why the reported 75% gas share plus 15% royalty on Jangal-e-Kalan are shares of something that does not exist yet; the five thresholds between signature and treasury — capital actually spent, output produced, output measured by someone the state trusts, a buyer who pays in money through a visible channel, and a collector who banks the state's share — and that missing one makes the other four worthless; coal as the worked example, the one mineral that reliably earned hard currency at $9.9m in June 2025 alone and whose export earnings were zero in every month from November 2025 to June 2026 once Pakistan shut its crossings, failing at threshold four rather than at geology; where mining sits in the accounts, which is nowhere — the World Bank's revenue tables carry tax, customs and non-tax only, the named non-tax drivers being road and transport tolls, passport and administrative fees, overflight charges and railway and telecom receipts, and the last ministry collection figure is AFN 13.2bn from August 2022 against AFN 227.8bn of total state revenue in ten months of FY2025; the announcement record (2023 seven contracts $6.5bn, Nov 2024 three $1.2bn, Jan 2025 nine ~$2.9bn, and eighteen small 2025 contracts worth ~$24m, the small ones being the ones that became holes in the ground), with AAN's judgement that the real impact and timeline 'are however difficult to ascertain' and the Aynak and Hajigak precedent; measurement as the deepest problem, the last national mineral survey having been Soviet in 1977; and the conclusion that Afghan revenue grows from fees on movement and paperwork — non-tax up 29% while customs fell 24.7% with the border shut — rather than from rocks
